gaps.sentence: Her suitcase was ___ , so the airline charged extra (WEIGHT).
gaps.hint: weighing too much — that is why she paid extra (over-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means too much: overweight explains the extra charge.

gaps.sentence: The training course will ___ you to work abroad (QUALIFY).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: qualify. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: She apologized for the ___ caused by the delay (CONVENIENT).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed — the delay was a bad thing
gaps.explanation: A delay causes inconvenience (negative prefix in- + noun); the sentence needs the noun, not the adjectives.

gaps.sentence: The audience found the lecture extremely ___ (BORE).
gaps.explanation: The lecture causes boredom, so it is boring; the audience would be bored.

gaps.sentence: She is very ___ in modern art (INTEREST).
gaps.hint: how she feels: -ed; fixed pattern '___ in'
gaps.explanation: 'Interested in something' describes the person's feeling; 'interesting' describes the thing that causes it.

gaps.sentence: The festival celebrates ___ (CREATE) in every form.
gaps.explanation: 'Celebrates creativity' — the abstract quality noun follows the verb.

gaps.sentence: She speaks English ___ for a beginner (REMARKABLE).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'speaks': remarkably (-ly).

gaps.sentence: The ___ (POPULAR) of the band grew after the film.
